column5: My phone had been dead for seven days.
Tonight, she plugged it in.
The last video on it was from day one.
I'm Mark. Chicago has been dark for a week.
I'm hiding in a tunnel under the city,
with a woman in a gray coat who says I'm on their list.
And I don't remember recording this.
Day one. Nine fourteen P M.
A rooftop. The whole skyline still lit.
Then a voice behind the camera. Mine.
Okay. Starting with the north side.
And the lights start going out.
Not all at once. Block by block.
Like someone is checking names off a list.
Toward us.
When the last tower goes dark, the camera flips around.
Six people on that roof. All in gray coats.
One of them is her.
And the one holding the phone,
is me.
I looked up at her.
You were never on their list, Mark.
You wrote it.
Above us, the grate scraped open.
Flashlights poured down the ladder.
And that calm voice from the radio called down.
Mark. Your shift started a week ago. Come home.
Every person in that tunnel turned to look at me.
And part of me remembered the way.
